raw_response:
I will keep the farm simple and spread risk. Because some people in my household work off-farm, I do not want a plan that depends on too much hand labor at the same time. I will put 5 mu into winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land, because that gives me stable grain and makes full use of irrigation. I will keep 5 mu in cotton, because I already know how to manage it and it still helps diversify income, but I will not expand it because it takes more field attention. I will put 4 mu into stevia, because it fits my current cropping pattern and can bring cash income, but I will limit the area so labor and management stay under control. I will use improved or hybrid seed where it matters for yield and stand establishment, apply moderate fertilizer instead of pushing too hard, irrigate based on crop need and my well access, and keep tillage practical with rotary tillage for most fields and ploughing for cotton where I want a better seedbed. My goal is steady output, manageable labor, and lower production risk across the year.
